body:
This is related to #471, which seems to miss part of the point. I would like to add detailed information of the actual problem.

## Expected Behavior

My temporal docker stack has two networks attached, because one of them is used to connect to a logging stack.

As I do not know the docker IP addresses in advance, and my server is connected to other nodes in my temporal cluster, I want my temporal service to listen to all IPs and publish the ports on the broadcasted IP (frontend example below, but all other services are configured the same way) :

```
global:
    membership:
        maxJoinDuration: 30s
        broadcastAddress: "X.X.X.X"  # my host routed address here

# [...]

services:
    frontend:
        rpc:
            grpcPort: 7233
            membershipPort: 6933
            bindOnIp: 0.0.0.0
            httpPort: 7243
```

In the temporal-server contaiiner, it should look like
```
$ netstat -tpln | grep 7233
tcp        0      0 :::7233                 :::*                    LISTEN      1/temporal-server
```

Other temporal services do that just well, for exemple temporal-ui, or even the metrics endpoint of temporal-server when configured like this : `listenAddress: "0.0.0.0:8080"` 

## Actual Behavior

```
$ ip a | grep "inet.*scope global"
    inet 172.20.0.3/16 brd 172.20.255.255 scope global eth0
    inet 172.18.0.2/16 brd 172.18.255.255 scope global eth1

$ netstat -tpln | grep 7233
tcp        0      0 172.20.0.3:7233         0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      1/temporal-server
```

Unfortunately, this is not the right IP.

## Some hints

When configured with `bindOnIp: 0.0.0.0`, when starting up, temporal server loops on all interfaces and tries to "guess" a unique IP to listen to ; see functions `ListenIP()` and `scoreAddr()` in `common/config/localip.go` :

```
// scoreAddr scores how likely the given addr is to be a remote address and returns the
// IP to use when listening. Any address which receives a negative score should not be used.
// Scores are calculated as:
// -1 for any unknown IP addreseses.
// +300 for IPv4 addresses
// +100 for non-local addresses, extra +100 for "up" interaces.
func scoreAddr(iface net.Interface, addr net.Addr) (int, net.IP) {
```

In my case, both networks have the same exact scoring, so only the first one listens to my service. As there is no way to order interfaces, this behaviour is random.

## Steps to Reproduce the Problem

  1. run a standard temporal stack
  2. configure `bindOnIP: 0.0.0.0`
  3. execute `temporal operator cluster health` in the temporal-admin-tools : OK
  4. attach another network to temporal-server, restart stack
  5. execute `temporal operator cluster health` in the temporal-admin-tools
````
time=2026-03-26T09:47:23.169 level=ERROR msg="failed reaching server: connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 172.18.0.2:7236: connect: connection refused\""
```

## Specifications

  - Version: temporalio/server:1.30.1
  - Platform: Linux Debian 12

This looks interesting. I will need to adjust my setup because I run temporal-server with a config file already setup (no env vars) but naming the interfaces can really help.

This could be a workaround, though I think the temporal-server implementation itself should not guess an IP address and really bind on all interfaces when told so ; just like temporal-ui does.

Anyways, thanks for your quick answers.

More info on that topic. When running temporal-server image with only env variables, the server actually binds on given `BIND_ON_IP` (i.e. all interfaces if 0.0.0.0 is passed)
The problem occurs when running the server with a config file via `TEMPORAL_SERVER_CONFIG_FILE_PATH`. This is when the previous code is triggered and tries to detect an IP to bind to.

> More info on that topic. When running temporal-server image with only env variables, the server actually binds on given `BIND_ON_IP` (i.e. all interfaces if 0.0.0.0 is passed) The problem occurs when running the server with a config file via `TEMPORAL_SERVER_CONFIG_FILE_PATH`. This is when the previous code is triggered and tries to detect an IP to bind to.

This explains a lot. `BIND_ON_IP` variable or `bindOnIP` in config file do work just fine. But I wrote a config file with the wrong `bindOnIp` key (wrong case) which just ignores this value and runs the interface scoring describe before.

Meaning that this issue is actually not a bug but a feature, though it is not obvious when we would need it.

title: Temporal server only bind on one interface even though "bindOnIp" is set to "0.0.0.0"
